subject: Route drift playbook + minimum sampling config request
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Route drift playbook + minimum sampling config request

Folks —

Following the Acme Cloud incident last week (OBS-4923), product asked for a small set of console changes we need to avoid repeated manual forensics. High level ask: make it straightforward for SRE/CS to detect customer-route drift in cost/latency profiles and capture a minimal sample (KV/cache + token-path) for 24–72h for postmortem without retaining full traces long-term.

Key pieces I'm proposing (attached: draft_playbook.md and sample_config.xlsx):
- A per-route "drift" signal that combines token-cost delta, median tail-latency shift, and model-variant swap rate.
- A UI affordance on the Route page: "Capture sampling window" (start/stop, TTL, retention class).
- Minimum sampling config to reduce storage (e.g., sample 1% of calls by default, increase to 5% for 6h when drift threshold crossed; store aggregated KV snapshots + 5 full calls per minute).
- Export links (signed GCS link) for CS/engineering to pull artifacts for escalations.

Why this is important now: we keep losing time to manual traces and ad-hoc redlines when a tenant hits a sudden cost/latency delta (often due to model change or prompt shift). If we can standardize a light-weight snapshot that includes representative token-paths + prefix cache stats, we can do triage within hours instead of days.

Questions for you:
1) Marcus — any infra blockers for implementing a short-lived snapshot and per-route sampling toggle?
2) Kimberly — can you validate the sample config sizes in sheet (storage/ingest roughs)?
3) Lauren — where would this land on product priorities? Is this triage > feature?
4) Jonas — any concerns re: telemetry schema changes or UX constraints?

Next step: can we sync tomorrow (30m) if you can all make it? If not, reply with notes and I'll collate.

Thanks,

Soojin Lee
Director, Observability & Product Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Route drift playbook + minimum sampling config request

+1 on the problem and nice concise ask. Quick infra notes:
- Short-lived snapshot is doable; best approach is to create an S3/GCS archive job that runs on-demand and uses lifecycle rules to delete after TTL. We shouldn't keep full traces in hot storage.
- Cost risk: if we increase sampling to 5% for any mid-size tenant, storage and egress can spike. We need a guardrail: per-tenant bandwidth cap + throttled export.
- Implementation effort: ~3 sprints to add the UI toggle + snapshot job + signed link flow if we do it correctly (auth+audit). We can scope an MVP: compressed artifacts, 24h TTL, per-route max of 100MB/day by default.

I'll add a short infra backlog item and estimate; Kimberly, can you sanity-check the numbers in the sheet?

-Marcus

Marcus Lin
VP Engineering, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 13:20:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Route drift playbook + minimum sampling config request

Soojin — looked through sample_config.xlsx. Quick summary:
- The proposed default 1% sample looks fine for text-generation heavy routes. For high-throughput embedding routes, 1% is still a lot; recommend route-type conditional defaults.
- Storage estimate: median tenant (20M tokens/day) at 1% with compressed token-paths ~ 120MB/day. If drift triggers 5% for 6h, add ~60–80MB for that window.
- Aggregated KV snapshots (small) are negligible compared to full call captures.

Concerns:
- Billing attribution: exports should not accidentally cause customer egress charges that are hard to reverse. We need explicit consent in some contracts.
- Data retention & compliance: if an export contains PII we need a quick redaction or a policy to block exports for regulated tenants. That should be on the playbook.

I'll mark items in the sheet with flags and propose route-type buckets (generation vs embeddings vs rerank).

-Kimberly

Kimberly Park
Technical Program Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jul 2028 15:06:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Route drift playbook + minimum sampling config request

Thanks all — this aligns with a couple product priorities: incident triage improvements and tenant isolation controls. Proposed approach from product side:
- MVP (Q3): per-route "Capture sampling window" button, default route-type buckets, compressed artifacts with 24h TTL, signed export links (read-only) routed through audit service.
- Post-MVP (Q4): configurable retention tiers, contract-level export permissions, and a lightweight drift alert tied to the console with recommended next steps.

Can Marcus and Kimberly confirm dependency list and rough effort by EOD Fri? I'll slot a 2-week investigation spike for this in the roadmap and add OBS-4923 to the priorities board.

Also, can someone volunteer to draft the playbook text for the public-facing help center? I can edit and publish.

-Lauren

Lauren Bishop
